page: Amazon Web Services r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz with 1 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor, contains no local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3077.67 and a strong bzip3 single-threaded decompression speed of 13.9 GB/sec. Text processing performance is also strong, scoring 2674.0 in Geekbench. However, multi-core operations, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the average tier. A notable hardware tradeoff is the memory bandwidth performance; while cached small-block reads are average at 592.0 GB/sec, uncached large-block reads are weak at 37.49 GB/sec. Similarly, LLM inference speeds for a medium 7B model are weak, though performance remains average for smaller 135M models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.xlarge offers a dense memory profile relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. Because it lacks local storage and has a modest 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, it is best suited for workloads relying on network-attached storage. Recommended workloads include in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing applications, and general-purpose memory-intensive enterprise applications.
